stories.title: New paper proposes WildAWM, a pipeline for training computer-use AI agents
stories.summary: A new paper introduces WildAWM, a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks to train general computer-use agents, addressing the risks of training such agents directly on real systems.
stories.more: The paper argues that agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world, but scaling that directly on real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce security risks. WildAWM is proposed as a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents. The authors note that existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction setting, which WildAWM aims to generalize beyond.

stories.title: Paper tackles KV-cache costs for long-running LLM agent trajectories
stories.summary: A new paper addresses how KV-cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost as LLM agent trajectories grow long, proposing cache engineering techniques that avoid invalidating cached states when trimming history.
stories.more: As LLM agents handle increasingly complex tasks, their trajectories of observations and actions grow long, making key-value cache I/O and storage the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed a model's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work used context engineering — trimming or summarizing history — to reduce cache size, but modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states. The paper proposes an approach to cache engineering that avoids this tradeoff.

stories.title: Future Chunk Prediction aims to fix shortcut learning in video generation
stories.summary: A new auxiliary training objective, Future Chunk Prediction, pushes autoregressive video diffusion models to truly model scene evolution rather than relying on temporal redundancy as a shortcut.
stories.more: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate video chunk by chunk, but producing plausible continuations does not guarantee they capture how scenes actually evolve over time. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy can let local visual continuity serve as a shortcut for denoising the current chunk, reducing pressure to model real visual evolution. Future Chunk Prediction (FCP) is introduced as an auxiliary objective, jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising, that predicts temporally separated future chunks instead.

stories.title: Socratic Skill Learning interleaves teaching and practice for agent skills
stories.summary: A new method, Socratic Skill Learning, has an AI Educator guide a Student agent through practice while the Student remains the sole environment operator and skill author, aiming for skills that transfer beyond the original task.
stories.more: Agent Skills make task knowledge reusable across sessions, but learning transferable skills requires evidence about a procedure and its conditions of use — evidence a single successful attempt can leave untested. Socratic Skill Learning (SSL) interleaves expert teaching with student practice to address this. An Educator guides investigation while the Student remains the sole environment operator and skill author, able to question, test, and adapt the Educator's advice. The method is designed to test skill reuse beyond the original task.

stories.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation unifies spatial, channel attribution
stories.summary: A new attribution method, Spectral-Spatial Interpretation, explains multispectral model predictions over position-channel pairs instead of separate spatial heatmaps and channel scores, which the authors say miss spatially localized channel relevance.
stories.more: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks via spatial heatmaps, or which channels matter via global channel scores — separate views the paper says are limiting for multispectral data, where channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI) is introduced as a full-grid attribution method over position-channel pairs. For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context and defines a conditional attribution for that position-channel pair.

stories.title: DONIC is a new generalist tracker for bimanual dexterous robot manipulation
stories.summary: A new paper presents DONIC, described as the first generalist bimanual dexterous tracker, jointly trained to handle the contact-rich, two-handed manipulation behaviors common in real life but underaddressed by prior single-hand models.
stories.more: Existing dexterous reference-tracking models focus mainly on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving common bimanual dexterous behaviors largely unaddressed. The paper attributes this gap to the scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the added complexity of coordinating contacts across two hands. DONIC is presented as the first generalist bimanual tracker, jointly trained across human demonstration data to handle these contact-rich, two-handed tasks.

stories.title: Study tests whether pre-training scaling gains transfer to virtual game worlds
stories.summary: A controlled study of 120 training configurations examines whether continued pre-training gains seen for embodied agents in physical environments also hold in virtual worlds with different visuals, dynamics, and objectives.
stories.more: Scaling data, diversity, and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences stay grounded in shared physical laws. The paper investigates whether these gains extend to virtual worlds that vary in visual style, dynamics, controls, and objectives. The study examines continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes — data volume, diversity, and model size — spanning 120 training configurations across four model sizes.

stories.title: Critical PHP RCE flaw found by AI tools gets exploited after disclosure leak
stories.summary: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 4 Argon independently found a critical PHP remote-code-execution flaw patched across PHP 8.x; a leaked disclosure let hackers exploit it for days before patches landed.
stories.more: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol discovered the flaw through its Patch the Planet initiative, while security firm Wiz independently found the same bug using Google's Gemini 4 Argon. The two CVEs began circulating on forums around 15:00 UTC on October 20th after a leak in the coordinated disclosure process, according to the PHP Foundation. Fixes landed across the entire PHP 8.x line, and the PHP Foundation says it is strengthening its security practices as a result. AWS logged exploitation attempts starting four days before patches shipped, and the bugs are now being broadly exploited across the internet. OpenAI noted that the same AI capabilities that find vulnerabilities can also help attackers exploit them.
